In what year was Tardigrade discovered?
Tardigrade: The earliest known fossil is from the Cambrian, some 500 million years ago.
Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-17: Russian Aircraft Corporation MiG. The MiG-17 was license-built in China as the Shenyang J-5 and Poland as the PZL-Mielec Lim-6.
NASA X-43: Boeing. The NASA X-43 was an experimental unmanned hypersonic aircraft with multiple planned scale variations meant to test various aspects of hypersonic flight.
Who is credited with discovering Phoenix?
Phoenix (constellation): Petrus Plancius. Named after the mythical phoenix, it was first depicted on a celestial atlas by Johann Bayer in his 1603 Uranometria.
Who is credited with discovering Glycerol?
Glycerol: Carl Wilhelm Scheele. Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.
Who is credited with discovering Theory of relativity?
Theory of relativity: Albert Einstein. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.
Who is credited with discovering Sombrero Galaxy?
Sombrero Galaxy: Pierre Méchain. It is a member of the Virgo II Groups, a series of galaxies and galaxy clusters strung out from the southern edge of the Virgo Supercluster.

Produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex, this mineralocorticoid is the body's key sodium-saver, quietly governing blood pressure and potassium balance in the kidney — which hormone is it?
Aldosterone is the main mineralocorticoid steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland.
This psychological term describes a diverse set of deficits in the ability to feel or anticipate pleasure, and is recognized as a diagnostic feature in the DSM-5 — what's the term?
Anhedonia is a diverse array of deficits in hedonic function, including reduced motivation or ability to experience pleasure.
Four novels and fifty-six short stories about a certain consulting detective made his name — but this knighted British writer-physician also invented Professor Challenger. Who was he?
Arthur Conan Doyle (22 May 1859 - 7 July 1930) was a British writer and physician.
Native to Europe, this small white-petaled, yellow-centered lawn flower is called 'common,' 'lawn,' or 'English' in various regions — what is its scientific name?
Bellis perennis (p-), the daisy, is a European species of the family Asteraceae, often considered the archetypal species of the name daisy.
This rigid, mineralized organ of the vertebrate skeleton produces both red and white blood cells and helps regulate the body's acid-base balance — what is it?
Bone is a rigid organ that constitutes part of the skeleton in most vertebrate animals.

What suborder of orthopteran insects — its Latin name meaning 'chisel-bearing,' after the stout shape of its members' egg-laying organs — includes grasshoppers, ground-hoppers, and pygmy mole crickets?
Caelifera are a suborder of orthopteran insects. The latter should not be confused with the mole crickets (Gryllotalpidae), which belong to the other Orthopteran suborder Ensifera.
Mature females are cows, the intact males are bulls, and the castrated males pull plows as oxen — all names for one widespread domesticated bovine kept as livestock. What animal is it?
Cattle (Bos taurus) are large, domesticated, bovid ungulates widely kept as livestock.
This roughly 24-hour internal biological cycle, generated within an organism but tuned by cues like daylight, is regulated by an internal biological clock — what is it called?
Circadian rhythm is a natural oscillation that repeats roughly every 24 hours.
Lending its metal to sterling silver, cupronickel coins, and strain-gauge alloys, this element carries atomic number 29 and a name drawn from the Latin 'cuprum' — what is it?
Copper is a chemical element; it has symbol Cu (from Latin cuprum) and atomic number 29.

This American nuclear physicist worked on the Manhattan Project and later led the Federation of American Scientists, best remembered for his 1959 testimony that helped sink a controversial cabinet nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill (November 11, 1919 - December 14, 2008) was an American nuclear physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project during World War II and was head of the Federation of American Scientists.
This scarab superfamily insect is famous for rolling balls of animal droppings, a behavior the Ancient Egyptians linked to the god Khepri — which creature is it?
Dung beetle are beetles that feed on feces.

This broad set of measures — taken by individuals, advocacy groups, and governments alike — aims to prevent pollution, conserve natural resources, and maintain ecological balance, sometimes repairing existing damage — what is it called?
Environmental protection refers to the taking of measures to protecting the natural environment, prevent pollution and maintain ecological balance.
A Swiss linguist and philosopher who died in 1913, this thinker's ideas shaped 20th-century linguistics, psychoanalysis, and anthropology alike, according to one of his translators — who is he?
Ferdinand de Saussure (26 November 1857 - 22 February 1913) was a Swiss linguist, semiotician and philosopher.

Discovered in Paris in 1875 and bearing the symbol Ga on the periodic table, this soft, silvery chemical element has such a low melting point — just below 30°C — that it turns liquid at warm room temperature. Name this element?
Gallium is a chemical element; it has symbol Ga and atomic number 31.

Five species of this group of plants — rice, wheat, maize, barley, and sugar cane — together cover 46 percent of the world's arable land, alongside two related families, sedges and rushes. What kind of plant is this?
Grass refers to various families of plants.
Which 19th-century American economist's wildly popular treatise Progress and Poverty argued that a single tax on the value of land could build a more just and productive society?
Henry George (September 2, 1839 - October 29, 1897) was an American political economist, social philosopher and journalist.

In this heart condition, muscle tissue — most often in the wall between the ventricles — thickens for no obvious reason, weakening the heart's pumping and sometimes its electrical rhythm — name the condition?
Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM, or HOCM when obstructive) is a condition in which muscle tissues of the heart become thickened without an obvious cause.

This Russian and Soviet physiologist discovered classical conditioning through famous experiments involving dogs, and won the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his separate research into digestion — who is he?
Holding doctorates in both anthropology and medicine, this SS physician earned the grim nickname 'Angel of Death' for his experiments and selections at Auschwitz — who was he?

Josef Mengele (16 March 1911 - 7 February 1979), often dubbed the "Angel of Death", was a German military officer and physician during World War II at the Soviet front and then at Auschwitz during the Holocaust.
This inflammation of the voice box causes symptoms ranging from a hoarse voice to complete voice loss, usually clearing up within two weeks. Name the condition?
Laryngitis is inflammation of the larynx (voice box). The primary symptom is loss of some vocal function, ranging from hoarse voice to no voice at all.
Used since pre-Columbian times as a pack animal that can haul about a quarter of its body weight for miles, which domesticated South American camelid has wool low in lanolin?
Llama (Spanish) (Lama glama) is a domesticated South American camelid, widely used as a meat and pack animal by Andean cultures since the pre-Columbian era.
Though it's the strongest bone in the face, this lower jawbone tends to deform with age and is prone to fractures — what is it called?

Mandible (from the Latin mandibula, 'for chewing'), lower jaw, or jawbone is a bone that makes up the lower - and typically more mobile - component of the mouth (the upper jaw being known as the maxilla).
Aristotle called this the 'first philosophy' — the branch that probes the most fundamental structure of reality, from existence itself to the categories of being — what is it?
Metaphysics is the branch of philosophy that examines the basic nature or most fundamental structure of reality.
Their name means "little fly" in Spanish, and biologists class them as micropredators — all sip flower nectar, but the females of many species also drink blood. What are they?
Mosquito are a family of small flies consisting of 3,600 species.

This Renaissance polymath put the Sun, not the Earth, at the center of the universe in a 1543 book published just before his death — likely arriving independently at an idea Aristarchus of Samos had floated eighteen centuries earlier. Who is he?
Nicolaus Copernicus (19 February 1473 - 24 May 1543) was a Renaissance polymath who formulated a model of the universe that placed the Sun rather than Earth at its center.
Many species in this cosmopolitan, often-fragrant family live as epiphytes on trees, and some have ditched leaves entirely — relying on highly specialized pollination tricks instead. What are they?
Orchid are plants that belong to the family Orchidaceae, a diverse and widespread group of flowering plants with blooms that are often colourful and fragrant.
This pulse crop, given the scientific name Pisum sativum by Linnaeus in 1753, is usually eaten as a vegetable via its small round seeds. What is it?
Pea is a pulse or fodder crop, but the word often refers to the seed or sometimes the pod of this flowering plant species.

A pnictogen with only one stable isotope and atomic number 15, this element hides in Earth's crust mostly as phosphate rock and readily builds a vast family of organic and inorganic compounds. Which element is it?
Phosphorus is a chemical element; it has symbol P and atomic number 15.
Part of the critical theory framework and closely tied to critical race theory, this field analyzes history, literature, and discourse shaped by imperial power — what field is it?

Postcolonialism is the academic study of the cultural, political and economic consequences of colonialism and imperialism, focusing on the impact of human control and exploitation of colonized people and their lands.

Found across Africa, Asia, and Australia, this family of nonvenomous snakes includes some of the world's largest and kills by coiling to suffocate rather than by injecting venom — what is the family called?

Pythonidae are a family of nonvenomous snakes found in Africa, Asia, and Australia. The taxonomy of pythons has evolved, and they are now known to be more closely related to sunbeam snakes and the Mexican burrowing python.
With a surface temperature over 12,000 Kelvin and a radius more than seventy times the Sun's, this blue supergiant is the brightest point of light in Orion — which star?
Rigel is a blue supergiant star in the equatorial constellation of Orion.
This systematic discipline builds testable explanations about nature and society, and is continuously challenged and validated by the community that practices it. What is it?
Science is a systematic discipline that builds and organises knowledge in the form of testable explanations about nature and society.
The brightest star in the night sky, this star sits in the constellation Canis Major and is actually a binary system paired with a faint white dwarf companion — name the star?
Sirius is the brightest star in the night sky, located in the southern constellation of Canis Major.

Held together by its own gravity, this luminous sphere of plasma is the type of object our Sun is, with roughly 4,000 of them visible to the naked eye on a clear night - what are these objects called?
Star is a luminous spheroid of plasma held together by self-gravity.
This genus of flowering plants in the daisy family is better known by the fluffy-seeded lawn weed it produces, with two European species now invasive nearly worldwide. What is it?
Taraxacum is a genus of flowering plants in the family Asteraceae which consists of species commonly known as dandelions.
This family of large, long-legged flies can be identified by a maxillary-palp segment longer than the other three combined, and typically has thirteen segments in each antenna. Name the family?
Tipulidae is a family of large crane flies in the order Diptera.
A physician before politics, this German served as Angela Merkel's defence minister and in 2019 became President of the European Commission — who is she?
Ursula von der Leyen (ne Albrecht; born 8 October 1958) is a German politician and physician who has served as President of the European Commission since 2019.
The first person to ever call himself a psychologist, this German founder of modern psychology launched Philosophische Studien, the field's first academic research journal — who is he?
Wilhelm Wundt (16 August 1832 - 31 August 1920) was a German physiologist, philosopher, professor, and one of the fathers of modern psychology.
The first Muslim scientist to win a Nobel Prize, this Pakistani theoretical physicist shared the 1979 Physics prize for unifying the weak and electromagnetic forces — who was he?
First flown in October 1972, this was the world's first twin-engine wide-body airliner, born from a 1967 France-West Germany-UK collaboration that later lost its British partner — what is it?
Airbus A300: World's first twin-engine widebody jet airliner.
Sold under the brand name Xanax, this fast-acting benzodiazepine is most often prescribed for panic disorder and generalized anxiety — what drug is it?
Alprazolam: Benzodiazepine medication. Alprazolam is most commonly prescribed in the management of anxiety disorders, especially panic disorder and generalized anxiety disorder (GAD).

Affecting about 1 in 15,000 people, this rare genetic disorder causes severe intellectual disability, little to no speech, and balance problems — yet those affected are often noted for a notably happy personality. Which condition is it?
Angelman syndrome: Genetic disorder caused by a mutation of chromosome 15.
Nicknamed the strawberry tree for its red berries, this evergreen Mediterranean shrub is the national tree of Italy — which plant?
Arbutus unedo: Species of flowering plant in the heather family.
Affecting roughly one in five people at some point and usually starting in childhood, this long-term itchy, red, cracked-skin condition is also simply called eczema — what's its formal name?
Atopic dermatitis: Long-term form of skin inflammation.
Belonging to genus Fagus, this deciduous tree yields timber used for furniture, flooring, and plywood, and its wood also makes excellent firewood. What is this tree?
Beech: Genus of trees in the family Fagaceae.
Predicted by Einstein's general relativity, this astronomical body is so compact that not even light can escape past its event horizon. What is it?
Black hole: Compact astronomical body. A black hole is an astronomical body so compact that its gravity prevents anything, including light, from escaping.
Named for the 18th-century French explorer who documented it on one of his expeditions, this thorny ornamental vine produces colorful bracts around three small waxy flowers — which plant is it?
Historically hardware-dependent in size, ranging anywhere from 1 to 48 bits, this unit of digital information now almost always means eight bits — what's it called?
Byte: Unit of digital information, usually 8 bits.
With the formula H2CO3, this fleeting compound has a lifespan of only about 20 milliseconds at body temperature before converting to water and carbon dioxide — which compound?
Carbonic acid: Chemical compound. The molecule rapidly converts to water and carbon dioxide in the presence of water.
Nicknamed 'no-see-ums' for their tiny 1-3mm size, these biting midges are also among the best-studied pollinators of cocoa plants — what is this fly family called?
Ceratopogonidae: Family of flies commonly known as no see ums, or biting midges.
Usually triggered when a gallstone blocks the cystic duct, this inflammatory condition causes right-upper abdominal pain that radiates to the shoulder — what is it?
The smallest member of the cockatoo family and native to Australia, this crested pet bird is kept in an estimated 4.8 million US households — what bird is it?
Cockatiel: Species of bird. It is, therefore, now classified as the smallest subfamily of the Cacatuidae (cockatoo family).
Nicknamed the shaggy mane or lawyer's wig, this scaly white mushroom dissolves itself into black ink just hours after being picked — which fungus?
Coprinus comatus: Species of fungus. The young fruit bodies first appear as white cylinders emerging from the ground, then the bell-shaped caps open out.

Commonly called sowbread, this genus of 25 tuberous flowering plants is prized for upswept petals and patterned leaves, native from the Mediterranean to Iran with one species even found in Somalia — which genus?
Cyclamen: Genus of flowering plants in the primrose family.
Caused by about 40 types of fungus and often picked up in public showers or contact sports like wrestling, this infection produces a red, itchy, scaly circular rash — what is it?
Dermatophytosis: Fungus infection of the skin. Dermatophytosis, also known as tinea and ringworm, is a fungal infection of the skin (a dermatomycosis), that may affect skin, hair, and nails.
Brought to Australia as an infant, this geologist joined Shackleton's Nimrod Expedition and became a leading figure of the Heroic Age of Antarctic exploration — who is it?
Douglas Mawson: Australian geologist and explorer of the Antarctic (1882–1958)

A subfield of physics and electrical engineering, this discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify current — and to convert AC to DC or analog to digital — what is it?

Electronics: Branch of physics and electrical engineering. The semiconductor industry is one of the global economy's largest and most profitable industries, with annual revenues exceeding $481 billion in 2018.
About 60 to 70 percent as sweet as table sugar yet virtually calorie-free, this sugar alcohol is fermented from corn and was commercially pioneered by Japanese companies in the 1990s — what is it?
Erythritol: Sugar alcohol that is used as a sweetener.
Sporting a dark facial mask and famous for a seriously foul-smelling territorial secretion, this stocky mustelid ranges across the continent and Morocco's Rif mountains — which species is it?
Belonging to the genus Abies, these evergreen conifers have cones that stand upright like candles and disintegrate at maturity, and some varieties serve as Christmas trees — which conifer genus?
Fir: Genus of coniferous trees. The genus is most closely related to Keteleeria, a small genus confined to eastern Asia.
Often bonded to glucose to form sucrose, this simple sugar is found in honey, fruit, and most root vegetables — which sugar?
Fructose: Simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants.

Among the longest of all living crocodilians, this fish-eater wields a slender snout lined with 110 interlocking teeth, and the males sport a bulbous, pot-shaped bump on the tip that gives the animal its name. What is it?
Gharial: Crocodilian native to the Indian subcontinent.
The seeds of five plants in this family, including rice, wheat, maize, barley, and sugar cane, cover 46% of the world's farmland — what group of plants is this?
Grass: Collective name for three families of plants.

This prehensile, multi-fingered body part sits at the end of primates' forelimbs — koalas famously have two opposable thumbs on each one, while raccoons are often said to have them despite lacking true opposable thumbs. What is it?
Hand: Extremity at the end of an arm or forelimb.

First synthesized in 1940 by chemist Roger Adams via hydrogenation of THC isomers, this psychoactive cannabis-derived compound is sold in vaporizers despite never being drug-approved — which compound?
Lightest and most abundant element in the universe, it makes up about 75% of all normal matter and fuels the stars — colorless, odorless, and highly combustible. What element is it?
Hydrogen: Chemical element with atomic number 1 (H)

Also known as the spectacled or binocellate snake, this reptile from South Asia is one of the 'Big Four' species responsible for most snakebites in the region and is revered in Hindu mythology — which snake?
Indian cobra: Species of snake. The species is native to the Indian subcontinent, and is a member of the "Big Four" species that are responsible for the most snakebite cases in Sri Lanka and India.
Awarded a gas-attack Iron Cross in WWI before sharing the 1925 Nobel with Gustav Hertz for the laws of how an electron strikes an atom — who was this German-American physicist?
Hailed as a 'miracle worker' in 1955, this researcher refused to patent his polio vaccine so it could spread worldwide for free — who is he?
Jonas Salk: American inventor of the polio vaccine (1914–1995)
Made from shredded pastry dough layered with cheese and soaked in sugar syrup, this Arab dessert is especially popular during Ramadan, with a famous variant hailing from Nablus — what is it?

One of the five big cats in the genus Panthera, this slender, muscular predator wears dark spots clustered into rosettes and is split today into eight recognised subspecies across Africa and Asia — what is it?
Leopard: Species of cat native to Africa and Asia.

This American stealth strike fighter comes in three flavors — conventional, short-takeoff/vertical-landing, and carrier-based — and with 883 in service is the world's fourth-most-numerous military aircraft. What is it?

Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II: American stealth multirole fighter aircraft. The Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II is an American family of single-seat, single-engine, supersonic stealth strike fighters.
With the formula MgCl2, this colorless salt forms hydrates and serves as the principal precursor to large-scale production of its namesake metal — what is it?
Magnesium chloride: Inorganic salt: MgCl2 and its hydrates. It forms hydrates MgCl2·nH2O, where n can range from 1 to 12.
Widely brewed as a calming herbal tea despite limited clinical evidence for its effects, this annual plant in the daisy family goes by the nickname 'scented mayweed' — which plant?
Matricaria chamomilla: Species of flowering plant.
First isolated in 1921 and encoded by the codon AUG, this essential amino acid also serves as the precursor to cysteine — which amino acid is this?
Native to Southeast Asia, this evergreen tree's leaves are known as kratom, containing alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors — which species?
Mitragyna speciosa: Species of plant. It is under preliminary research for possible antipsychotic and antidepressant properties.

Named for being quieter than its relatives, this large white waterfowl carries an orange beak topped with a black knob that's bigger in males, and is more common in North America than in its native Europe — which bird?
Mute swan: Large species of waterfowl. The mute swan (Cygnus olor) is a species of swan and a member of the family Anatidae within the waterfowl order.
Also known in everyday speech as 'brain surgery,' this medical specialty treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and the entire nervous system — what is it called?
Neurosurgery: Medical specialty of disorders which affect any portion of the nervous system.
This medical condition, defined by a body mass index over 30, is linked to heart disease, type 2 diabetes and sleep apnea — what is it?
Obesity: Medical condition of excess body fat.
This paired female gonad releases egg cells and secretes hormones that regulate the menstrual cycle and fertility — which organ?
Ovary: Female reproductive organ that produces egg cells.
One of the 20th century's most prolific mathematicians, this Hungarian championed Ramsey theory and famously preferred cracking open problems to building grand theories — who was he?
Found naturally in mammals' milk and a direct precursor to phenethylamine, this is one of nine amino acids your body can't make, so you eat it in meat, eggs, and legumes — which one?
This egg-laying Australian mammal hunts with its eyes, ears, and nostrils shut, sensing prey by electrolocation — and, oddly for a mammal, it's also venomous. What is it?
Platypus: Species of mammal. Like other monotremes, the platypus has a sense of electrolocation, which it uses to detect prey in water while its eyes, ears and nostrils are closed.
This New World family within the order Carnivora encompasses raccoons, ringtails, coatis, and kinkajous, most of them omnivorous — what family is it?
Procyonidae: Family of mammals. Procyonidae ( PROH-see-ON-i-dee) is a New World family of the order Carnivora.
Native to southern China, this pear tree's fruit goes by dozens of names worldwide - Asian pear, apple pear, nashi pear - but is rarely baked into pies due to its high water content - which species?
Pyrus pyrifolia: Species of pear with round crisp grainy fruit.
Rooted in Minangkabau cooking at the crossroads of the Malacca Strait, this dish slow-cooks meat in spiced coconut milk until the oil separates and it fries in its own glaze — what is it?
The second woman ever to win the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine — and the first American-born one — this physicist shared the 1977 award for developing the radioimmunoassay. Who was she?
Rosalyn Sussman Yalow: American medical physicist (1921–2011)

First used in English in the early 15th century and possibly named after a Mediterranean island, this term covers small oily forage fish under 15 centimeters, with larger ones called pilchards — what's the fish?
Sardine: Common name for various small, oily forage fish.
Domesticated more than 3,000 years ago and prized for having one of the highest oil contents of any seed, which crop is also known as benne?
Sesame: Plant cultivated for its edible seeds.

Once extracted from the ashes of certain salt-absorbing plants and now produced from ordinary salt and limestone via the Solvay process, this alkaline compound is also known as washing soda or soda ash — what is it?
Sodium carbonate: Chemical compound. Sodium carbonate (also known as washing soda, soda ash, sal soda, and soda crystals) is the inorganic compound with the formula Na2CO3 and its various hydrates.
Also known as asteroids for belonging to the class Asteroidea, this marine invertebrate typically has a central disc and five arms — what is it?
Starfish: Class of echinoderms, marine animal.
Also called the broadbill, this large migratory predator sports a long, flat, pointed bill and can reach nearly 15 feet in length — what fish is it?
Swordfish: Fish which has a long, pointed bill. Swordfish are elongated, round-bodied, and lose all teeth and scales by adulthood.
More than 30,000 unsaturated hydrocarbons built on (C5H8)n units, produced mostly by plants (especially conifers) and used by some insects as defense — what class of natural compounds is this?
Terpene: Class of oily organic compounds found in plants.
Arrested 36 times and branded "the most dangerous man in America" by Nixon, this Harvard psychologist founded a Psilocybin Project and became the face of psychedelic advocacy — who was he?

Once grimly nicknamed the "white death" and historically called consumption, this contagious bacterial disease usually starts in the lungs — and most who carry it never show a single symptom. What is it?
Tuberculosis: Infectious disease. Tuberculosis initially infects the lungs, but it can also spread to other parts of the body.
Heading the office that ran nearly all of America's WWII military R&D, this engineer launched the early Manhattan Project and later drove the creation of the National Science Foundation. Who was he?

This German American aerospace engineer and space architect (1912–1977) initially worked in Nazi Germany's rocket development program and later led rocket and space technology development in the US — who is he?
Wernher von Braun: German American aerospace engineer (1912–1977). The V-2 became the first artificial object to travel into space by crossing the Kármán line on 20 June 1944.
This citrus fruit of Chinese origin is believed to be a natural hybrid of a wild mandarin subspecies and the ichang papeda — what fruit?
Yuzu: Citrus fruit and plant. Yuzu (Citrus × junos, from Japanese 柚子 or ユズ;) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.

Sodium is denoted by which symbol?
The symbol for sodium is Na. Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na and atomic number 11.
